Subject: VPC SAN policy & proxy termination consent

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. To keep momentum toward your POC and the Dedicated deployment, we've pulled together a short proposal for how TLS and FQDN ownership would work for Acme's private VPC endpoints. High level asks:

- Please confirm whether Acme wants TLS terminated at your edge (customer-managed load balancer) or if you prefer Redwood's private proxy to terminate and present Redwood-managed certs for our internal FQDNs.
- Confirm the SAN naming policy below so we can generate initial certs and coordinate rotation windows.

Attached: redwood-proposed-san-policy.md (policy + allowed patterns), acme-tls-infra-sketch.png (diagram showing options A/B).

Proposal excerpt:
- SAN namespace: *.acme.private.example.com for application endpoints; service-specific CNs allowed for mTLS client auth.
- Rotation cadence: 90-day rolling certs for edge-presented certs; 30-day rotation for client certs used by Acme-managed services.
- Revocation and emergency rotation: 2-hour emergency rotation SLA when an active compromise is suspected (Redwood will push cert updates via our control plane and provide CSR handoff instructions).

If you prefer termination at Acme's edge, we will provide a CSR template and recommended OCSP/CRL endpoints. If Redwood proxies TLS, we need formal consent for Redwood-held private certs for the following internal FQDNs so we can route and SNI-map properly.

Next steps: Can you review and confirm over email or mark changes in the attached doc? If helpful, I can set up a 30-min call w/ Karthik (infra) and Neha (security) to walk through the sketch and agree on rotation SLAs.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for sending. A couple of quick clarifications from our side after an initial read:

- Security team prefers TLS termination at our edge where possible. We have strict mTLS requirements between our internal services and expect mutual TLS for any service-to-service traffic originated inside our VPC.
- For traffic from Redwood (control plane to Acme-managed endpoint), we need Redwood to present a cert chain we can validate against our in-house CA root. We do not want Redwood to present public CA certs for internal-only FQDNs.
- Rotation windows: procurement wants to avoid operational churn — can we standardize to 60-day rotations for web-facing certs and 30 days for client certs?

Attached: acme-cert-policy.pdf (our internal certificate policy).

We are generally OK with Redwood hosting a proxy if: (1) certs are issued by our CA (via CSR you generate), or (2) Redwood supports passthrough so we maintain end-to-end TLS.

I copied our security and procurement leads to make sure the appropriate approvals are in thread.

Best,
Tara
Tara Lim
Head of Infrastructure Security
Acme Payments

Attachment stub: acme-cert-policy.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: VPC SAN policy & proxy termination consent

Tara / Marissa —

Thanks for the notes, Tara — this is helpful. A few technical recommendations from our infra/security side:

1) Termination model options (pros/cons):
   - Edge termination (Acme LB): Full control to Acme; end-to-end TLS preserved; Redwood will route to the Acme FQDN via VPC peering or private link. Requires Acme to manage certs and OCSP/CRL availability.
   - Redwood private-proxy termination: Redwood terminates TLS at our private proxy inside your VPC; Redwood can present a cert signed by either (a) Acme's private CA (we accept CSR), or (b) a Redwood-managed cert signed by a private intermediate that Acme trusts. Proxy termination allows better caching and request-level routing but introduces a trust boundary that must be explicitly accepted.

2) SAN naming and SNI mapping:
   - We recommend using a small set of wildcard SANs to limit certificate churn (example: *.acme.private.example.com), and then additional specific names for service endpoints that require client cert binding.
   - Important: if Redwood will map multiple customer FQDNs to a single proxy IP, we need explicit SNI mapping docs from Acme to avoid cross-tenant TLS overlap.

3) mTLS and client cert rotation:
   - For mTLS we support both embedded client certs and a dedicated PKI integration. Rotation API: Redwood can pull new client certs from a predefined S3 HTTP(s) endpoint that Acme controls, or Acme can push certs to our control plane (preferred for audited delivery).

Operational asks from us:
- If Acme chooses Redwood proxy termination using Acme CA, please provide the CA root certificate and a CSR acceptance window (we will generate CSRs and return signed certs within 24 hours).
- For passthrough model, please confirm your LB health-check endpoints and TLS ciphers allowed — we will only present ALPN h2 and the following cipher suites: AES256-GCM-SHA384, CHACHA20-POLY1305.

I can join a technical call on Thursday (9/9) 10:00-10:30 PT to finalize SNI map and the CSR handoff.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
